questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: At morning assembly the school bell is struck with a wooden mallet and the sound is heard right across the playground. Consider the following statements. 1. A metal is a suitable choice for the bell because a metal gives out a sound when it strikes a hard surface. 2. The metals that produce a sound on striking a hard surface are said to be sonorous. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

evidence:
The metals that produce a sound on striking a hard surface
are said to be sonorous. Can you now say why school bells are made of
metals?

a sound?

options.C: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
options.D: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A student clamps a copper wire on a stand, fixes a pin to its free end with wax and heats the wire with a spirit lamp near the place where it is clamped. After some time the student finds that the wire is still in the solid state and has not melted. Consider the following statements. 1. The copper wire does not melt while it is being heated. 2. The wire stays solid because copper is a poor conductor of heat. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: A student is preparing a chart of metals for a school exhibition and writes on it that every metal is a solid at room temperature, and also that mercury is one of the metals that conduct heat best. Consider the following statements. 1. Every metal exists as a solid at room temperature. 2. Mercury is among the best conductors of heat. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are false.

evidence: (i) All metals except mercury exist as solids at room temperature.

The best conductors of heat are silver and
copper. Lead and mercury are comparatively poor conductors of heat.
